input.strategy_title: Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview and adoption is strong, but enterprise
customers will not build production GenAI applications on a TP component.
Graduating to GA requires API stability commitments, a production support
posture, and closing the quality gaps that TP status currently excuses. The
full inventory of those gaps is not yet known — TP feedback is scattered across
support tickets, and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. |
| HLR-3 | P0 | Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. |
| HLR-5 | P1 | The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). |
| HLR-6 | P2 | Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- TrustyAI
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- New Llama Stack feature development beyond GA-bar quality work
- Deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths

## Open Questions

1. The GA scope itself depends on HLR-1's assessment — until it lands, the
   size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

# Llama Stack GA-readiness gap assessment

## Description

This investigation resolves the strategy's defining unknown: the full inventory
of gaps between Llama Stack's current Tech Preview quality and the GA bar. TP
feedback is scattered across support tickets and no systematic GA-readiness
assessment has been done. The assessment consolidates that feedback, inspects
the current API surface and error handling, examines upgrade-path and
scale-limit evidence, and produces the definitive GA scope that all downstream
Llama Stack hardening work is planned against.

## Scope

- Consolidate Tech Preview feedback from support tickets and other TP feedback
  channels into a single gap inventory.
- Audit the current state of the four GA-bar dimensions named by the strategy:
  API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error handling.
- Classify each inventoried gap by GA impact (blocks GA, should fix, defer)
  with a stated rationale for inclusion in or exclusion from GA scope.
- Produce the definitive GA scope document, replacing the strategy's
  provisional estimate of the stability and hardening work's size.
- Convert each in-scope gap into scoped downstream work (acceptance criteria
  or work items) so the API-stability and support-posture efforts can consume
  it directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written gap inventory exists covering all four GA-bar dimensions (API
  stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), with each gap
  traceable to a TP feedback record, code/API inspection, or test evidence.
- Every inventoried gap is classified as GA-blocking, non-blocking-but-in-scope,
  or deferred, with a recorded rationale.
- A definitive GA scope document is produced and is specific enough that the
  API stability work and the production support posture work can be sized and
  planned from it without re-deriving the analysis.
- Follow-up items discovered during the assessment are recorded as scoped work
  items or acceptance criteria rather than left as prose.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP
  quality and the GA bar, producing the definitive GA scope.

## Risks / Notes

- Scale-limit and upgrade-path verification require a live cluster running the
  Llama Stack distribution; plan for cluster time during the assessment
  window.
- Sign-off of the definitive GA scope is a product decision — the technical
  inventory this epic produces is the input to that decision.

# Llama Stack API stability guarantee and tested upgrade path

## Description

This epic delivers the published API stability guarantee for Llama Stack as
required for GA: a versioned API surface, a deprecation policy, and a tested
upgrade path from the last two Tech Preview releases. Enterprise customers
will not build production GenAI applications on APIs without stability
commitments, so this work converts the TP-era API surface into one a GA
release can stand behind.

## Scope

- Version the published API surface of the Llama Stack distribution (the
  OpenAI-compatible REST APIs and the LlamaStackDistribution CRD surface).
- Author and publish a deprecation policy describing how API changes are
  announced, phased, and removed across releases.
- Implement and automate verification of the upgrade path from each of the
  last two TP releases to the GA release.
- Remediate the API-stability gaps that the GA-readiness assessment assigned
  to this surface (or record their explicit deferral with rationale in the GA
  scope).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published API surface is versioned, and the versioning scheme is
  documented.
- A deprecation policy is published covering announcement, phase-out, and
  removal of API changes.
- Automated upgrade verification exists and passes for upgrading a deployed
  distribution from each of the last two TP releases: given a distribution
  deployed at a prior TP release, when it is upgraded to the GA release, then
  existing API consumers continue to function within the stability guarantee,
  with any breaking changes covered by the deprecation policy.
- Every API-stability gap assigned to this epic by the GA-readiness assessment
  is either remediated or explicitly deferred with a recorded rationale.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): published API surface carries a stability guarantee — versioned
  APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP
  releases.

## Risks / Notes

- The size of this work is an estimate until the GA-readiness assessment
  lands; this epic is gated on that assessment and its scope may be rewritten
  by its findings.
- API surfaces originate upstream (meta-llama/llama-stack); changes to
  upstream API contracts may require midstream coordination or upstream
  contribution.

# Llama Stack production support posture (SLOs, backport policy, supported configuration matrix)

## Description

This epic puts the production support posture in place for Llama Stack GA:
documented SLO targets, a backport policy, and a supported configuration
matrix. This is the operational commitment set that distinguishes a supported
GA component from a Tech Preview one, and it is a distinct work product from
the API stability engineering — it is support-policy authoring plus
configuration validation, reviewed by product and support stakeholders rather
than code review.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the production support posture of
  Llama Stack distributions.
- Define and document the backport policy: which releases receive fixes, for
  how long, and how backports are requested and delivered.
- Build the supported configuration matrix enumerating the provider, storage,
  and deployment configurations that are supported at GA, validated to the
  extent the GA-readiness assessment's scale-limit and error-handling
  findings require.
- Incorporate the scale limits identified by the GA-readiness assessment into
  the matrix as documented, supported limits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets are documented and reviewed by the accountable stakeholders.
- The backport policy is documented, covering supported release lines, fix
  duration, and the backport request path.
- The supported configuration matrix exists, enumerates supported
  configurations, and every entry is either validated or explicitly marked
  with its validation status and limitations.
- Scale limits identified by the GA-readiness assessment are reflected in the
  matrix as documented limits, and error-handling expectations from the
  assessment are covered by the posture documents.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P0): production support posture is in place — documented SLO
  targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix.

## Risks / Notes

- SLO targets and the backport policy require product and support-organization
  sign-off; budget review time.
- The configuration matrix's scope is gated on the GA-readiness assessment's
  scale-limit findings and may be rewritten by them.

# TrustyAI guardrails as a supported Llama Stack integration

## Description

This epic promotes safety guardrails via TrustyAI from an experimental flag to
a supported, documented integration for GA Llama Stack distributions. TrustyAI
already ships fairness/bias, drift, explainability, and guardrails services in
the platform; the GA requirement is that wiring guardrails into a Llama Stack
distribution is a supported configuration path with documentation, not an
experimental opt-in.

## Scope

- Replace the experimental-flag enablement of the TrustyAI guardrails
  integration with a supported configuration path for Llama Stack
  distributions.
- Validate the integration end to end: a Llama Stack distribution configured
  with TrustyAI guardrails applies guardrails as documented.
- Author integration documentation covering configuration, supported
  deployment shapes, and known limitations of the guardrails integration.
- Confirm the integration is covered by the platform's standard support
  posture (no experimental disclaimers on the supported path).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Llama Stack distribution can be configured with TrustyAI guardrails
  through a supported (non-experimental) configuration path.
- End-to-end verification passes: guardrails are applied to requests on the
  configured distribution as documented.
- Integration documentation exists covering configuration, supported
  deployment shapes, and limitations, with no experimental-status disclaimers
  on the supported path.
- The integration is listed as supported for GA distributions in the
  Llama Stack supported configuration matrix (the
  support-configuration document delivered by the Llama Stack
  production support posture workstream) and in this epic's
  integration documentation.
- The prior experimental-flag enablement path remains functional
  through a documented transition window, and the supported
  configuration path can be reverted or disabled via configuration
  without code changes (rollback/feature-flag reversibility for the
  enablement replacement).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions.

## Risks / Notes

- The work spans TrustyAI (integration enablement, operator surface) and the
  Llama Stack distribution wiring; the TrustyAI team owns the integration
  deliverable and coordinates with the Llama Stack owning team on the
  distribution side.
- The "listed as supported" acceptance criterion depends on the Llama Stack
  supported configuration matrix, which is authored in parallel by the
  Llama Stack production support posture workstream (same owning team,
  different workstream). The TrustyAI team must coordinate its matrix entry
  with that workstream; the entry lands when both the integration and the
  matrix are ready.

# Dashboard Llama Stack management enabled by default for entitled clusters

## Description

This epic enables Llama Stack management in the Dashboard by default for
entitled clusters, removing the Tech Preview opt-in gate. Today users must
explicitly opt in to see Llama Stack management surfaces; at GA, entitled
clusters get those surfaces out of the box.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard's Llama Stack management enablement so that it is on
  by default for entitled clusters, driven by the Dashboard's per-component
  feature-flag/default configuration mechanism.
- Remove the Tech Preview opt-in gate for Llama Stack management.
- Preserve entitlement-aware behavior: non-entitled clusters do not show
  Llama Stack management surfaces.
- Retain a configuration path for administrators to disable Llama Stack
  management where the default is not wanted (reversibility of the default
  change).

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster with default configuration, Llama Stack management
  surfaces appear in the Dashboard with no manual opt-in.
- On a non-entitled cluster, Llama Stack management surfaces remain
  unavailable.
- The Tech Preview opt-in gate for Llama Stack management no longer exists in
  the configuration surface.
- An administrator can disable Llama Stack management via configuration, and
  the documented default can be reverted without code changes (feature-flag
  rollback for the default-on change).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P1): the Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for
  entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate).

## Risks / Notes

- The change alters default user-visible behavior; the rollback/feature-flag
  acceptance criterion above covers reverting the default.

# Llama Stack GA documentation uplift and TP migration notes

## Description

This epic uplifts Llama Stack documentation to GA standards, including
migration notes from Tech Preview. The documentation describes the GA feature
set that the implementation work delivers — the stabilized and versioned API
surface with its deprecation policy and tested upgrade path, the production
support posture, the supported TrustyAI guardrails integration, and default
Dashboard enablement — so it is authored after those implementations land.

## Scope

Content outline (to be finalized against the delivered GA feature set):

- GA overview and support-status documentation for Llama Stack (removal of
  Tech Preview disclaimers from the supported surface).
- API documentation reflecting the versioned API surface and the deprecation
  policy.
- Migration guide with notes from Tech Preview releases, covering the tested
  upgrade path from the last two TP releases and any behavior changes.
- Documentation of the production support posture: SLO targets, backport
  policy, and the supported configuration matrix with documented scale
  limits.
- Documentation of the supported TrustyAI guardrails integration for GA
  distributions.
- Documentation of default Dashboard enablement for entitled clusters,
  including how administrators disable it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Llama Stack documentation meets GA standards and covers the full GA feature
  set with no Tech Preview disclaimers on supported surfaces.
- Migration notes from Tech Preview are published, covering the upgrade path
  from the last two TP releases.
- All documentation is technically reviewed against the delivered
  implementations (review recorded per topic).
- The documentation set covers the supported guardrails integration, the
  support posture, and default Dashboard enablement.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-6 (P2): documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration
  notes from TP.

## Risks / Notes

- Priority is derived from the strategy-level Critical rating per the
  docs-authoring priority exception, not from HLR-6's P2 label; the epic is
  structurally last regardless.
